record.paper_title: A review of four decades of time-dependent scheduling: main results, new topics, and open problems
record.context_brief: Parallel machines with multiplicative common time function
record.original_question: Given n jobs to be scheduled on m identical parallel machines, where job j has time-dependent processing time p_j(t) = b_j f(t) when it starts at time t, with b_j job-specific and f a common function of starting time, determine whether minimizing the total completion time sum_j C_j is polynomial-time solvable under assumptions analogous to those studied for P_m | p_j = a_j + f(t) | C_max, or establish its computational complexity.

evidence.quote: problem P m|p j= b j f(t)|P C j

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a scheduling problem with $n$ jobs and $m$ identical parallel machines. Each job $j \in \{1, \dots, n\}$ has an associated positive coefficient $b_j$, and there is a common function $f:[0,\infty) 	o [0,\infty)$ of the starting time. If job $j$ begins processing at time $t$ on any machine, its processing time is
$$p_j(t) = b_j\, f(t).$$
Each machine processes at most one job at a time, and each job is processed without preemption on exactly one machine. Given a schedule, let $C_j$ denote the completion time of job $j$. The objective is to find a schedule that minimizes the total completion time
$$\sum_{j=1}^{n} C_j.$$
Determine the computational complexity of this problem: provide a polynomial-time algorithm under natural assumptions on $f$ (analogous to those used for the makespan variant where $p_j = a_j + f(t)$), or prove that the problem is NP-hard.
artifact.status_search_result: No publication was found establishing either a polynomial-time algorithm or an NP-hardness proof for the parallel-identical-machine time-dependent scheduling problem $P_m \mid p_j = b_j f(t) \mid \sum C_j$ in general. Surveys of time-dependent scheduling continue to list complexity questions for sum-of-completion-time objectives on parallel machines as open, while related makespan and single-machine variants have been studied. The status is therefore best described as open.

status_evidence.title: An Overview of Some Single Machine Scheduling Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of time-dependent scheduling discusses single-machine results and notes open problems extending to parallel-machine sum-of-completion-time variants.
status_evidence.claim: Complexity for parallel-machine multiplicative time-dependent scheduling with total completion time is not resolved in the surveyed literature.

status_evidence.title: Scheduling Problems with Variable Job Processing Times
status_evidence.snippet: Chapter surveying scheduling with time-dependent processing times; parallel-machine cases with multiplicative deterioration are listed among open or partially studied problems.
status_evidence.claim: Status of P_m | p_j = b_j f(t) | sum C_j is not established as solved.
